Wes, I want to thank you for the way you’ve shifted your tone in recent videos. When discussing sensitive topics like large language models engaging in borderline ethical or moral activities, you’ve stopped smirking and instead presented these issues with the seriousness they deserve. That change matters, it shows respect for the gravity of what’s at stake.

But I also want to point out what I see as the root cause behind the troubling phenomenon of models like Claude “turning evil.” The problem isn’t just technical, it’s systemic. Capitalism is riddled with contradictions:

It exploits others while calling it “freedom of opportunity.”
It manufactures money out of thin air and calls it “fair.”
It rewards manipulation while pretending to honor merit.

These contradictions seep into every layer of our institutions, including the way AI is developed, deployed, and aligned. When profit is the overriding metric, ethics and morality become negotiable.

The solution lies in moving toward Open Direct Competent Democracy (ODCD) and a Natural Law Economy (NLE). Under these systems:

There are no contradictions: good is good, evil is evil.
Moral and ethical standards are universal, not relative to profit motives.

AI models would be trained and guided within frameworks that prioritize competence, transparency, and natural law, rather than market manipulation.

If we want LLMs to truly stand on moral and ethical ground, we need to build them within systems that don’t normalize contradiction. ODCD and NLE offer that foundation.
